name: Communication notifications and conversations
plain: Shows who a message is from with their photo, tied to the system's contact graph.
meaning: Links alerts to a person so Focus can allow only certain people through. It also feeds the system's idea of who the user talks to; apps declare the intent for each message.

android.prompt_ui: Conversation space in the shade; bubbles toggle
android.note: Conversation shortcuts publish contacts to the launcher

ios.prompt_ui: Contact avatar and name in the banner
ios.note: Needs a service extension to update the content with the intent

limits.headline: Can show who a message is from, with their photo, in the alert
limits.user_action: You allow notifications and get a message from someone in your contacts
can: Show the sender's name and picture in the alert banner
Group chats into a conversation space on Android
Share frequent contacts with the launcher on Android so you can reach them fast
cannot: Do this on iPhone without Apple's approval for communication notifications
See your whole contact list just because it shows one sender's photo
Show up if you turned off notifications for the app
limits.reach_label: Only the people in your messages
limits.differs: iPhone needs an Apple approved entitlement and an extension to add the sender. Android uses conversation shortcuts and bubbles.

story.what_it_is: Alerts that show the sender's photo and name and connect to your contacts.

marketing.name: Communication notifications
marketing.pitch: Apple lets messaging apps show alerts with a contact's picture and name, and work with Focus filters.

story.for_you: You see your friend's face and name on the alert. Focus modes can let that person through while blocking everyone else.
story.for_makers: Makers get messages that feel personal and are easy to answer. The system also learns who you talk to most, which helps ranking and suggestions.

use_cases.example: A message from your sister shows her photo, so you spot it on the lock screen.
A social app shows a person you follow in your notifications.
A work chat app shows the teammate name and lets Focus allow only your boss.
A dating app shows a match picture on a new message alert.
A game with chat shows which friend sent an invite to join a match.
A family app shows which child sent a message to a parent.
Messages read out in the car use the sender name.

risks: Builds a map of who you talk to
Photos shown on the lock screen
story.android_note: Android groups chats in a conversation area and supports bubbles.
story.ios_note: iOS needs a service extension and special permission to show the contact image.

technical_bounds: Android bubbles can be disabled by the user

abuse: Social graph building via donated intents
